HomePage.whyText: Heat matters too — but it's more expensive, slower and harder to verify. Electricity gives us a foothold: it's visible on the meter, it reacts quickly to changes, and it's felt in the wallet.

whyItems.title: Measurable
whyItems.text: The meter shows kilowatt-hours every day. There's a 'before' and 'after' to compare, not a guess. This data builds a calculation you can verify.

whyItems.title: Faster than other solutions
whyItems.text: Equipment is installed in days or weeks, not a season. No scaffolding, no weather dependency, no disruption to the building's life.

whyItems.title: Visible on the bill
whyItems.text: The result shows up in the next payment document. That matters when a board makes the decision: people see what they paid for.

whyItems.title: Life support
whyItems.text: A battery storage system keeps critical loads running during outages: lighting, pumps, communications, elevators. Insulation alone never provides that.

HomePage.whyFooter: This doesn't cancel out thermal modernization. It comes as the next stage — once the consumption profile is clear, there's something to confirm the effect with, and a way to fund the co-owners' contribution.
HomePage.segmentsText: A community, a business, an HOA, a developer, a donor and a private owner all face different constraints: ownership form, decision-making, access to financing and consumption patterns. One-size-fits-all doesn't work here — so each segment has its own entry point.

segments.text: Energy diagnostics, procurement support, grant readiness, feasibility studies and energy management for communities and municipal utilities.

segments.title: Business & industry
segments.text: Cut costs, prepare an investment project, assess BESS feasibility, improve energy resilience.

segments.title: HOAs
segments.text: Solar and storage for the building, metering, financing programmes, then thermal solutions.

segments.title: RES / BESS developers
segments.text: DSO interaction, technical conditions analysis, financial model, specification and investor-ready decisions.

segments.title: Donors, NGOs, investors
segments.text: Evidence-based projects, a structured project package, a portfolio of opportunities and a bridge to the community on the ground.

segments.title: Private owners
segments.text: Solar and storage for a home — from calculation to a working system, turnkey.

HomePage.competenciesText: A full cycle in one circuit — from measurement to a working system confirmed by metering data. What is usually torn between different contractors, we pull together.

competencies.title: Survey and measurement
competencies.text: Consumption profile, load patterns, metering status, connection capacity, heat loss. The baseline data without which any calculation is just a guess.

competencies.title: Calculation and modeling
competencies.text: Sizing generation capacity and storage capacity to the actual profile. Payback assessment based on current tariffs, not average figures.

competencies.title: Design solutions
competencies.text: System architecture, equipment composition, connection scheme, stage sequencing. A technical specification you can take to a contractor or a financing program.

competencies.title: Turnkey implementation
competencies.text: Procurement, partner contractors, compliance control against the design, sign-off and result verification against metering data. Coordination between participants sits with the Center, not with the client.

nodes.label: Solar
details: Generates energy during the day, depending on sunlight
Capacity is sized to the consumption profile, not the roof area
Surplus is either stored or fed back into the grid

nodes.label: Storage
details: Stores surplus generation and off-peak tariff energy
Lifespan is measured in cycles, not years

nodes.label: Load
details: The consumption profile determines what's even worth installing
Without measuring the profile, the payback calculation is unreliable

nodes.label: Control
details: Decides when to charge, when to discharge, when to draw from the grid
Accounts for the tariff, generation forecast, and connection limits
Without this layer, equipment operates blindly

nodes.label: Metering
details: Records what's consumed and what's fed back into the grid
The basis for settlements with the supplier
Metering data is the starting point of any energy audit

nodes.label: Grid
details: The distribution system operator, the connection point
Connection capacity limits everything that can be installed
Grid feed-in terms are set by contract

OsbbPage.metaDescription: Thermal modernization financing programs for HOAs: terms, requirements, contacts and course of action.
OsbbPage.title: Financing for HOAs
OsbbPage.intro: The fastest results for an apartment building come from electricity projects: own generation, storage, and consumption management. Thermal modernization comes next — it's more expensive and pays back slower. Below are the programs currently operating in Ukraine, with their terms, requirements and contacts. We verify the data and note the check date.

whyItems.title: Measurable
whyItems.text: The meter gives daily data. The effect can be calculated, not just estimated by eye.

whyItems.title: Fast
whyItems.text: Installation takes days or weeks, no scaffolding and no seasonal dependency.

whyItems.title: Tangible
whyItems.text: The result shows up on the next bill — that's clear to a board of co-owners.

whyItems.title: Life support
whyItems.text: A battery keeps lighting, pumps and communications running during outages.

OsbbPage.programsText: Program terms change. Before applying, it's worth calling the administrator to confirm the current status.
OsbbPage.stepsText: The sequence is roughly the same for all programs.

steps.title: Capture the consumption profile
steps.text: How much, when, and on what electricity is spent. Without this data, solar and storage capacity are sized by guesswork, and the payback calculation is unreliable.

steps.title: Check connection capacity
steps.text: The grid operator contract terms limit what can be installed at all and how much can be fed back into the grid.

steps.title: Hold a co-owners' meeting
steps.text: A board decision is required for any program — grant or loan. No application is accepted without minutes.

steps.title: Prepare documents
steps.text: Cost estimate, design documentation, HOA financial statements, association registration documents.

steps.title: Set the work sequence
steps.text: Start with what pays off fastest: metering, generation, storage, load management. Thermal modernization comes as the next stage.

steps.title: Choose a funding source
steps.text: A grant, a loan, or a combination. The choice depends on the scope of work and the HOA's ability to cover its own share.

steps.title: Apply and support the project
steps.text: After approval — choosing a contractor, quality control of the work, reporting to the program.

reminders: The information on this page is for guidance only. Final terms are set by the program administrator.
Submitting an application doesn't guarantee approval. The decision is made by the program's committee.
We don't publish approval statistics or savings examples we can't back with a source.
Before making financial decisions, we recommend confirming the terms directly with the program administrator or bank.

AboutPage.intro: The Center for Energy Efficiency in Ladyzhyn works with community facilities, businesses, HOAs and private owners: it surveys, calculates, designs solutions and carries them through to a working system — ourselves or with partner contractors, while the expert, technical and technological role stays with the Center.

principles.title: Measurement first
principles.text: No recommendation is made without baseline data. Consumption profile, metering status, connection capacity — that's where any work begins.

principles.title: Solutions built for the site
principles.text: No two sites are alike. What paid off in one building might not pay off next door due to a different consumption pattern or grid limits.

principles.title: Sequence, not everything at once
principles.text: Work is broken into stages by speed of payback. Metering and electricity first, then thermal solutions and building envelope work.

principles.title: Verifiability
principles.text: The effect is confirmed by metering data after implementation. Every figure we publish has a source and a check date.

AboutPage.channelsText: The website is one channel, not the service itself. The real work happens on site and in the project materials.

CitizensPage.heroText: Solar panels, energy storage, smart control — we size everything for your home, consumption profile, and roof. Lower your electricity bills, gain energy independence, keep the lights on during blackouts.
CitizensPage.whyText: For a private house, an energy project isn't a trend — it's a smart way to cut utility costs and have power when the grid goes down.

whyItems.title: Lights on during blackouts
whyItems.text: The battery backup powers your home when the grid fails. Fridge, lights, pump, gas boiler — everything works as usual.

whyItems.title: Pay less for electricity
whyItems.text: Solar generates during the day when you're home or at work. Storage captures that energy and powers the house at night cheaper than buying from the grid.

whyItems.title: Earn from extra power
whyItems.text: On sunny days, panels produce more than you need. The surplus feeds into the grid — the utility pays you under your agreement.

CitizensPage.solutionsText: Not everyone needs everything. We explain how to combine components to fit your needs and budget.

solutions.title: Solar + net metering
solutions.text: Panels generate during the day. Surplus feeds to the grid — you receive payments from the utility.

solutions.title: Solar + battery storage
solutions.text: Panels generate, battery stores it. At night you power the house with your own energy — no grid fees.

solutions.title: Solar + battery + backup
solutions.text: Complete independence — during blackouts the battery powers you, during the day panels charge, at night you use stored energy.

solutions.title: Battery only without solar
solutions.text: If location doesn't allow panels — a battery charges from the grid at night rates and powers the house during the day at cheaper cost.

CitizensPage.stepsText: From first consultation to turning on the lights — 2-4 months depending on complexity and weather.

steps.title: Consultation
steps.text: We discuss your home, roof, and electricity bills from the past year. We determine what's actually possible.

steps.title: Roof survey
steps.text: We inspect your roof, take photos, assess orientation, shade from neighbors, and usable area for panels.

steps.title: Usage profile analysis
steps.text: We analyze your bills to see when you use the most energy, and how to combine generation and storage optimally.

steps.title: Preliminary calculation
steps.text: Equipment cost, installation complexity, expected annual savings. We calculate exactly how many years until payback.

steps.title: Design documentation
steps.text: We prepare connection drawings, diagrams, and calculations. Everything the utility and installers need.

steps.title: Installation & connection
steps.text: We install panels, meter, battery, control system. We coordinate with the utility and bring your system online.

steps.title: Training & support
steps.text: We explain how to use the system, what to watch for in the app, when to call for maintenance.

CitizensPage.ctaTitle: Ready to see what it costs?
CitizensPage.ctaText: Tell us about your home, how many people live there, estimated roof area — we calculate the cost and show payback period.

CommunityPage.heroText: For community centers, hospitals, schools, non-profits — we develop solutions accounting for public property specifics, grant opportunities, and energy independence needs.
CommunityPage.whyText: For public facilities, energy projects work differently than private sector. There are grants, but also bureaucracy. We understand both.

whyItems.title: We understand public property
whyItems.text: Decision-making is different: you need tenders, reports, approvals from authorities. We know how to structure a project so it gets approved.

whyItems.title: We know the grant programs
whyItems.text: Public facilities have special support programs. We help identify which conditions fit your facility.

whyItems.title: We ensure energy independence
whyItems.text: Medical clinics, hospitals, evacuation centers need reliable power. We design systems that work 100% during blackouts.

CommunityPage.objectsText: Each facility type has different constraints. We design solutions for what you have.

objects.title: Medical facilities
objects.text: Clinics, practices, small hospitals — need backup power for equipment and refrigeration.

objects.title: Educational institutions
objects.text: Schools, gymnasiums, training centers — are heavy energy users with flexible schedules and heating load shifting options.

objects.title: Community centers
objects.text: Community centers, libraries, civic buildings dramatically cut utility costs through energy projects.

objects.title: NGOs & volunteer centers
objects.text: Organizations working with distributed energy gain autonomy with solar, focusing on their mission instead of electricity bills.

CommunityPage.ctaText: Tell us about your facility, how many people use it, and current energy costs — we'll help identify the most effective solution.

BusinessPage.heroText: We survey your facility, calculate ROI, design solar, storage, and energy management systems. Scale from 10 kW to several MW to match your needs.
BusinessPage.whyText: For businesses two metrics matter: production cost and stability. On-site generation delivers both.

whyItems.title: Reduces production cost
whyItems.text: Electricity costs more at night and peak hours. On-site generation during the day, storage charging at night rates — baseline electricity cost.

whyItems.title: Protects from blackouts
whyItems.text: When the grid fails, generation switches to local system. Critical equipment runs, production doesn't stop.

whyItems.title: Calculate with real numbers
whyItems.text: ROI is based on your actual consumption profile, not averages. You see exactly how many years until payback.

BusinessPage.scenariosText: Each business has its own schedule and constraints. Here are common problems — here's how to solve them.

scenarios.title: Generation and consumption offset in time
scenarios.text: Production runs at night, solar generates only day. Battery stores daytime generation to power nighttime operations.

scenarios.title: Connection power limits
scenarios.text: The grid operator won't allow higher connection power. Local systems handle peaks, grid supplies base load.

scenarios.title: Critical load during blackouts
scenarios.text: Equipment is designed for continuous operation — blackouts cause losses. A backup system switches in milliseconds to generation.

scenarios.title: Understand which projects pay back fast
scenarios.text: Some facilities are built such that energy projects pay back in 1-2 years. Others take 5. We calculate exactly for each site.

BusinessPage.ctaText: Describe your production type, consumption volumes, and grid constraints — we'll prepare a preliminary calculation.

ServicesPage.heroTitle: A result, not advice and a folder of documents
ServicesPage.heroText: We see it through to the end — ourselves or with partner contractors, while the expert, technical and technological role stays with the Center. You deal with a single window: survey, calculation, design, procurement, implementation and result verification — inside one circuit of responsibility.
ServicesPage.windowTitle: One circuit instead of five contractors
ServicesPage.windowText: An energy project is usually torn between different contractors: one surveys, another calculates, a third designs, a fourth installs — and none of them answers for the final result. The Center pulls this into a single circuit.

window.title: One point of responsibility
window.text: You talk to the Center, not to five contractors. Coordinating the stages is our job, not yours.

window.title: The expertise stays with the Center
window.text: Where hands are needed, we bring in partner contractors. The expert, technical and technological role stays with us: we set the requirements, control execution and sign off the work.

window.title: We close with a result
window.text: A project ends not with a folder handed over, but with a working system whose effect is confirmed by metering data.

ServicesPage.formatsText: By default we carry a project through to the result. But if you only need an idea checked or a single stage covered — that's a normal way in too.

formats.title: One-off consultation or expert opinion
formats.text: For a quick check of an idea, a risk or a specific decision.

formats.title: Retainer
formats.text: For regular monitoring, analytics, procurement or regulatory support.

formats.title: Project support
formats.text: For a specific stage: audit, feasibility study, specification, grant, procurement, connection or financial model.

formats.title: Turnkey project
formats.text: From the first survey to a working system. Complex energy, investment and infrastructure projects requiring cross-disciplinary coordination and partner contractors.

formats.title: Strategic partnership or consortium
formats.text: For long development programmes, building a project portfolio and joint participation in grant or investment initiatives.

ServicesPage.productsText: These are stages inside a turnkey project. Each can be taken separately if you have the rest covered — but by default we don't stop at any of them.
ServicesPage.priceNote: Cost and timelines are set by scope after an initial conversation. There is no standard price list: scope depends on the state of the site, the data available and how deep we go.

ServicesPage.digitalText: A project doesn't end when the equipment is switched on. For the result to be visible every day rather than once a year in a report, the site needs metering that collects data and a system that shows it and lets you act. If there isn't one, we set it up. If there is one but it doesn't work, we rebuild it.

digital.title: Modern metering systems
digital.text: Setting up or upgrading metering: devices, data collection, hourly consumption and generation profile. Without it, any effect is a guess, not a fact.

digital.title: Online tracking and control
digital.text: Live data from the site: consumption, generation, battery state, deviations from normal. Alerts when something goes wrong — before it shows up on the bill.

digital.title: Analytics for management
digital.text: Dashboards and reports that show exactly where the losses are, how the equipment performs and whether the result matches the calculation. For a director, a board or a donor — in plain form.

digital.title: Applications built for the project
digital.text: Software tools developed and adapted to a specific site, client and their processes. Not a generic panel like everyone else's, but something your people will actually use.

digital.title: Energy management system implementation
digital.text: Energy management as an ongoing process, not a one-off audit: policy, owners, indicators, regular review. Oriented on ISO 50001 logic, scaled to the size of the site.

ServicesPage.digitalFooter: The digital circuit is what makes the promise "we close with a result" verifiable. It is from its data that we confirm the effect after implementation.

DevelopersPage.heroTitle: A bridge between the investment and the site
DevelopersPage.heroText: The developer brings capital, intent and deadlines. On the ground there is a grid operator, contractors, a community and real constraints. The Center stands between them: technical, documentary and technological support from technical conditions to a working system, with a guarantee that what's on paper matches what's on site.
DevelopersPage.bridgeText: A RES or BESS project rarely fails on equipment. It fails on grid connection, technical conditions, an unrealistic financial model and a contractor nobody controlled. That is exactly what we carry across the bridge.

guarantees.text: The Center sets the technical requirements and signs off the work. One criterion: as in the specification, not "as it turned out". The contractor knows they will be checked.

guarantees.title: Adaptability
guarantees.text: The solution is fitted to real constraints: connection capacity, grid regime, site condition, budget. A copy of the neighbour's configuration doesn't work here — and we don't offer it.

guarantees.title: Realism
guarantees.text: We take on what can actually be connected, built and maintained. If a project won't fly, we say so at the analysis stage — not after design money has been spent.

DonorsPage.heroTitle: A bridge between funding and the community on the ground
DonorsPage.heroText: A donor, NGO or investor needs an evidence-based project, a structured package and confidence that money turns into a result, not a report. The Center stands between funding and the place: prepares the project package, holds the technical and documentary expertise, controls contractors and returns verified data about the result.
DonorsPage.bridgeText: The most common problem of a donor project is the gap between what's written in the application and what exists on site. We know the place, so the package we prepare matches the community's reality.

PrivacyPage.label: Legal
PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.intro: This policy explains what personal data the website of the Center for Energy Efficiency (Ladyzhyn) collects, why, for how long, and what rights you have. We collect only what is needed to reply to your request.

sections.title: Who processes the data
paragraphs: The controller of personal data is the Center for Energy Efficiency, Ladyzhyn, Vinnytsia region (the Center). Contact details are on the Contacts page.

sections.title: What data we collect
paragraphs: We process only the data you provide yourself on the site — via the request form, the assistant chat, or when registering a knowledge-base account:
items: your name or how to address you;
the type of your organisation or site (e.g. HOA, business, community);
the text of your request and, for chat requests, the conversation with the assistant;
the page the request was sent from and the interface language.

sections.title: Why we process it
paragraphs: The only purpose is to handle your request: contact you, clarify the situation and suggest where to start. The legal basis is your consent, given by ticking the box in the form or sending a contact in the chat.
We do not use your data for mailings without separate consent and do not pass it to third parties for advertising.

sections.title: The assistant on the site
paragraphs: The assistant replies based on the site's materials. If the Center has an external language model connected, the text of your message may be sent to that model's provider to generate a reply. Do not enter passport data, card numbers or other sensitive information in the chat — it is not needed to answer your question.

sections.title: Knowledge-base account
paragraphs: If you register, we store your email, name and organisation (optional), your password as an irreversible hash (bcrypt), your plan and the date of your last sign-in. To enforce plan limits we keep a count of consultant requests (date and request type) without storing the questions themselves beyond your session.
Sign-in uses a technical session cookie valid for up to 30 days or until you sign out. The account can be deleted on request together with all related data.

sections.title: Paid services and invoices
paragraphs: If you order a paid service or plan, we process the payer's name and details, the amount and the issue and payment dates in order to issue an invoice. This data is kept for as long as accounting law requires (at least three years after the reporting period). The site does not collect or store bank card details.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: The site uses no advertising or tracking cookies. Only technical preferences are stored in your browser: the chosen theme, language and the current assistant conversation within a session, so it does not disappear between pages. This data does not leave your device.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Requests are kept as long as needed to handle them and communicate about your project, but no longer than three years from the last contact unless the law requires otherwise. Spam and erroneous requests are deleted.

sections.title: Who has access
paragraphs: Only authorised Center staff have access to requests. Technical services (hosting, database, mail server) may be used to store data and send emails; they process data on behalf of the Center and may not use it for their own purposes.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the Law of Ukraine "On Personal Data Protection" you have the right to:
items: know what data of yours we process and receive a copy;
To exercise any of these rights, write to us via the Contacts page form or the email listed there. We reply within 30 days.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy. The current version is always published on this page with the update date.

PrivacyPage.contact: Questions about personal data — via the Contacts page form, marked "personal data".

TermsPage.label: Legal
TermsPage.title: Terms of Use
TermsPage.intro: By using the website of the Center for Energy Efficiency you agree to these terms. They are simple: the information on the site is for reference, decisions about your site are made after a survey, and the assistant on the site is not a substitute for a specialist.

sections.title: What this site is
paragraphs: The site describes the Center's areas of work, the process and ways of working, and lets you leave a request. The site is not a public offer: the terms of specific cooperation are set by a separate agreement after discussing your task.

sections.title: Informational nature
paragraphs: All descriptions of services, stages and financing programmes are for reference. We verify programme data and indicate the verification date, but programme conditions change — check them directly with the programme administrator or bank before making financial decisions.
We do not publish figures we cannot back with a source, and we do not publish case studies without the client's written consent.

sections.title: The assistant on the site
paragraphs: The assistant replies based on the site's materials and does not invent figures, prices or timelines. Its replies are not a technical opinion, a commercial offer or legal advice. Decisions about your site are made after a survey and a conversation with a Center specialist.

sections.title: Requests
paragraphs: By sending a request you confirm that the contact details belong to you and agree that the Center will contact you to handle the request. Personal data processing is described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: Intellectual property
paragraphs: The texts, diagrams and design of the site belong to the Center. You may quote the site's materials with a reference to the source. Commercial use without the Center's consent is not permitted.

sections.title: Liability
paragraphs: The Center makes every effort to keep the information accurate and current, but does not guarantee uninterrupted operation of the site and is not liable for decisions made solely on the basis of information from the site without consulting a specialist.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We may update these terms. The current version is always published on this page with the update date.

TermsPage.contact: Questions about the terms — via the Contacts page form.

ProjectsPage.metaDescription: What the client receives at each stage of working with the Center and how the result is confirmed — by metering data, not a report.
ProjectsPage.heroText: We don't publish case studies without the client's written consent or figures without a source. Instead we show exactly what you receive at each stage — and how we make sure the working system delivers the effect that was in the calculation.
ProjectsPage.artifactsTitle: What the client receives at each stage
ProjectsPage.artifactsText: Not an abstract consultation but a concrete product you can present to management, a donor, an investor or a procurement team.

artifacts.title: Short energy profile
artifacts.text: Where the losses are, what consumes most, what the load pattern is. The starting point for any decision.

artifacts.title: Expert opinion
artifacts.text: An answer to a specific question: does it make sense, what are the risks, what next. Brief and to the point.

artifacts.title: Technical specification
artifacts.text: Solution architecture, equipment composition, requirements for works. A document you can take to a contractor.

artifacts.title: Feasibility study
artifacts.text: A feasibility study with a financial model, scenarios and risks — for a management or investor decision.

artifacts.title: Grant application
artifacts.text: Project concept, budget, impact logic, a full material set in the format of a specific programme.

artifacts.title: Procurement package
artifacts.text: Procurement plan, specification, market analysis, documents, deadline control — without errors or delays.

artifacts.title: DSO interaction package
artifacts.text: Technical conditions analysis, connection risks, action plan, documents for the grid operator.

artifacts.title: Financial model
artifacts.text: Operating modes, payback scenarios, tariff sensitivity — on the actual profile, not averages.

artifacts.title: Analytics dashboard
artifacts.text: Consumption, generation, battery state, deviations — online, for a director, a board or a donor.

artifacts.title: A working system confirmed by metering data
artifacts.text: The project closes not with a folder handed over, but with equipment that works and meter readings that match the calculation.

ProjectsPage.proofText: The effect must be visible on the meter, not in a presentation. So measurement is both at the start and at the end.

proof.title: We measure "before"
proof.text: Consumption profile, metering status, connection capacity — before any works. Without this baseline, "savings" remain a guess.

proof.title: We sign off against the specification
proof.text: One acceptance criterion: as in the specification, not "as it turned out". The contractor knows the result will be checked.

proof.title: We compare "after"
proof.text: Metering data after commissioning against the calculation. If they diverge, we find out why and fix it — instead of writing a report.

ProjectsPage.casesNote: Real case studies with figures will appear on this page once the data is confirmed by metering and clients give written consent to publication. This is our rule, not a placeholder.

hub.principlesTitle: Three rules of the knowledge base

principles.title: Verified by a person
principles.text: Every document card and every digest passes through a Centre specialist. The date of the last check is on the card.

principles.title: Continuously updated

principles.text: The consultant answers only from documents in the base and shows which ones it relies on. No link — no answer.
